10 Bidirectional typechecking, in which terms either synthesize a type

17 tional approach to polymorphism, however, are less obvious. We
18 give a declarative, bidirectional account of higher-rank polymor-
19 phism, grounded in proof theory; this calculus enjoys many proper-
20 ties such as η-reduction and predictability of annotations. We give
21 an algorithm for implementing the declarative system; our algo-
22 rithm is remarkably simple and well-behaved, despite being both
23 sound and complete.

28 Bidirectional typechecking (Pierce and Turner 2000) has become
29 one of the most popular techniques for implementing typecheck-

32 perti et al. 2012); subtyping (Pierce and Turner 2000); intersec-

36 2007; Dunfield 2009); refinement types for LF (Lovas 2010); con-
37 textual modal types (Pientka 2008); compiler intermediate repre-
38 sentations (Chlipala et al. 2005); and object-oriented languages in-
39 cluding C♯ (Bierman et al. 2007) and Scala (Odersky et al. 2001).
40 As can be seen, it scales well to advanced type systems; moreover,
41 it is easy to implement, and yields relatively high-quality error mes-

60 the normalization of intuitionistic type theory, in which normal

62 ing, and neutral (or atomic) terms correspond to the synthesis
63 mode. This enables a proof of the elegant property that type anno-
64 tations are only necessary at reducible expressions, and that normal
65 forms need no annotations at all. The benefit of the proof-theoretic
66 view is that it gives a simple and easy-to-understand declarative ac-
67 count of where type annotations are necessary, without reference to
68 the details of the typechecking algorithm.
69 While the proof-theoretic account of bidirectional typecheck-
70 ing has been scaled up as far as type refinements and intersection
71 and union types (Pfenning 2008), as yet there has been no com-
72 pletely satisfactory account of how to extend the proof-theoretic
73 approach to handle polymorphism. This is especially vexing, since
74 the ability of bidirectional algorithms to gracefully accommodate
75 polymorphism (even higher-rank polymorphism) has been one of
76 their chief attractions.
